result.title: SWE-Shift: Evaluating Coding Agents in Evolving Workspaces
result.summary: Repository-level coding benchmarks largely assume that tasks and environments remain unchanged throughout execution. In software development, code, dependencies, runtime state, and requirements can change while an agent is still working. We introduce SWE-Shift, a benchmark for evaluating coding agents under such mid-execution changes. From the same saved history and workspace, a Clean continuation proceeds without intervention, while a matched Shifted continuation receives a task-relevant update. Success requires completing the current task, preserving still-valid work, and satisfying the applicable state and evidence checks. The benchmark contains 120 scenarios across 12 change families, each evaluated at nine scheduled intervention positions. We evaluate 17 coding-agent systems, all of which have lower Shifted than Clean success. GPT-6 Astra drops from 67.35% to 24.79%, with 20.34% paired success. Tool/session changes and stale evidence yield zero paired success across all systems. Late-position paired success is lower for some systems and higher for others. These results show that success on the unchanged task can coexist with failures to preserve work, recover state, or refresh evidence after an update.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SWE-Shift 基准：在编码 agent 执行过程中注入与任务相关的环境变更，覆盖 120 个场景、12 类变更与 9 个干预位置，比较 Clean 与 Shifted 续跑，发现 17 个系统在变更后成功率普遍下降，并暴露出工作保留、状态恢复与陈旧证据刷新上的失败。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「陈旧证据」检查与执行中状态更新设定，可能为 LVR 多轮推理中视觉证据何时刷新、哪些既有中间结论仍可保留，以及是否重启或继续的判断提供评价思路，可供核查。
